feature: HTTP/2 WebTransport listener connection handshake budget and capacity recovery

behavior.budget: Options.connection_timeout defaults to 10 seconds; one absolute awake timestamp starts after TCP acceptance and spans TLS/ALPN, HTTP/2 bootstrap, EndpointServer creation and connection-table installation
behavior.idle_accept: waiting for a new TCP peer does not consume that peer admission budget
behavior.phase_caps: shorter configured TLS and HTTP/2 handshake deadlines retain their existing caps
behavior.ownership: acceptOwnedStreamWithDeadline consumes the accepted socket on entry, including validation, cancellation and bootstrap failures; existing validation-before-transfer accepted-stream APIs retain their contracts
behavior.expiry: owner allocation cannot regain Session operation_timeout; failed installation does not publish the endpoint or mutate the reserved slot, and rollback requests abortive owner shutdown before releasing the reservation
behavior.capacity: a timed-out handshake releases its reserved connection capacity and the listener continues to accept healthy peers
behavior.structure: separate listener connection ownership module and HTTP/2 owning admission helper, with nearby unit and socket tests

targeted_debug.command: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='HTTP/2 owned stream admission' -Dtest-filter='HTTP/2 TLS server caller timeout' -Dtest-filter='HTTP/2 accepted TLS stream timeout' -Dtest-filter='WebTransport HTTP2' --summary all

regressions: idle TCP listener followed by a silent cleartext peer closes that peer and admits a healthy HTTP/2 connection using the one slot
silent pre-TLS peer closes under the listener budget; a subsequent authenticated TLS/h2 peer is admitted

a deterministic one-second clock advance after HTTP/2 bootstrap during first managed-owner allocation exceeds the 100-ms admission deadline, frees that owner, closes its socket and leaves no connected slot
expired/wrong-clock, contended-mutex and canceled connection installation preserve reserved/generation/owner fields
owning socket admission closes the transport exactly through validation/cancellation/callback failure and does not call bootstrap on invalid admission

independent Python peer holds silent pre-TLS, authenticated missing-preface and authenticated partial-preface sockets with one worker/slot and a 250-ms budget; all close and the following Session exchanges exact stream, DATAGRAM and CLOSE

remaining_scope: Broader WebTransport browser/proxy coverage, gRPC Core integration policies and cross-protocol superiority evidence remain open; this evidence establishes listener connection admission behavior.
